For the exact legal rules, the full list of allowed names, and how to register a birth, use these official Portuguese Government resources.

These links open official Government of Portugal websites in your browser. Portugal's Approved Names is an independent app and is not official, endorsed by, or affiliated with the Portuguese Government or the IRN.

For unusual or borderline cases, the final answer always comes from the Portuguese civil registry / IRN.

The IRN (Portugal's civil registry authority) doesn't publish any list or flag identifying which names are considered "traditional" Portuguese names. This filter is only a best-effort approximation, not an official classification.
Treat this filter as a rough guide, not a definitive answer. Some traditional names may be hidden, and some hidden names may still be traditional.

As a best effort, a name is shown when it matches a curated list of well-known classic Portuguese names, or otherwise when it follows Portuguese spelling patterns: no K, Y or W; no "ph", "th", "sh" or "tz"; every "q" is followed by "u"; it doesn't start with "s" followed directly by a consonant; it doesn't end in a consonant other than "l", "r", "s", "z", "m" or "n"; and it has no doubled letters other than the native "rr"/"ss" — not even repeated vowels like "aa" or "ee".
